Unmodeled adhesive budget is not physical opaque coverage.
Each changed gap, baffle, slot, fin or support revision requires regeneration.

limitations: This short fore-bay foil is an explicit experimental part, not the fixed-motor multilayer assembly or an accepted TVC thermal solution.

The long-cylinder thermal approximation omits finite-end and angular bypass. Its short aspect ratio is a material validity limitation; no full thermal acceptance follows from a passing mean temperature.

The complete cap/ring/rail/body/root strength, compliant recovery, retained 50 g allowance and controller gates remain open.

limits: The same-time material-node temperature comparison isolates radiation geometry; it does not recalculate coupled wall surface temperatures, conduction, convection or temperatures.

Axisymmetric annuli retain actual foil thicknesses, segment ends, ring stations, thicknesses, bores and bond gaps, but fill angular fin slots/notches and omit sparse rails, sector spacers, seams and retention blocks. Neither a universal upper nor lower bound for complete CAD is claimed.

The diagnostic is truncated at the liner ends. The forward ring, forward thrust plate, aft retainer, nozzle and upper bay are missing boundary geometry, explicitly replaced by black end-reservoir sensitivity brackets.
Ambient and prescribed exterior-case temperatures bracket the assumed missing end-boundary radiosity; they are not measured data or a proof of actual nozzle/plume/end temperatures.
The original foil and mica are opaque; their touching cylindrical faces are removed from the radiation enclosure.
All foil surfaces retain the contaminated emissivity 0.9. No shield or radiation term is removed and the 45 C substrate screen remains unchanged.
Sampling intervals and convergence apply only to the stated geometric and diffuse-gray reduction. Material uncertainty, axial thermal gradients and physical verification remain open.
